blocks.text: Iran, exile, Afghanistan, Massoud: in his Paris studio, Reza recounts the encounters and convictions that run through his images.

Written, directed and edited by Guillaume Louyot , this independent documentary interview sets the photographer’s words in dialogue with his photographs. In about twenty minutes, it explores the trust that precedes the portrait, beauty in the face of suffering, and the responsibility of those who bear witness.
From uprooting to the bonds forged with Massoud, from the invisible wounds of war to transmission, the film draws the portrait of a man for whom looking at the world means a way of being with others.
“The essential quality of everything is empathy.” Reza, excerpt from the interview
Trust before the image. Taking the time to be accepted, preserving the person’s dignity, and knowing when to put the camera down.
Exile and memory. Iran, prison, uprooting, and the relationship with Massoud, nourished by poetry and games of chess.
Transmission. Giving women and young people the means to tell their own story through images.
